content: Stavudine, whether used alone or in combination with other antiviral medications, has the potential to cause severe and potentially fatal damage to the liver and pancreas. It can also lead to a life-threatening condition known as lactic acidosis. Inform your doctor if you have a history of liver or pancreatic disease, gallstones, or if you have been on long-term HIV treatment. Additionally, disclose if you consume or have consumed large amounts of alcohol, or if you are taking didanosine (Videx) or hydroxyurea (Droxia, Hydrea). If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, notify your doctor immediately. Should you become pregnant while taking stavudine, contact your doctor without delay. If you experience symptoms such as nausea, vomiting, unexpected or unusual abdominal pain, sudden weight loss, extreme fatigue or weakness, shortness of breath, rapid breathing, weakness in your arms or legs, or any sudden changes in your overall health, seek medical attention immediately. It is crucial to attend all scheduled appointments with your doctor and the laboratory, as your doctor will order specific tests to monitor your response to stavudine. Stavudine is prescribed in combination with other antiviral medications to treat HIV infection in patients with or without AIDS. It belongs to a class of antiviral drugs called nucleoside analogue reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NRTIs) and works by slowing the spread of HIV in the body. However, it does not cure HIV, prevent HIV-related illnesses, or stop the transmission of HIV to others. Stavudine is available as a capsule and an oral solution (liquid) to be taken by mouth, usually twice daily (every 12 hours), with or without food, and with plenty of water. To ensure consistent dosing, take it at the same time each day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take stavudine exactly as directed, without altering the dose or frequency. If administering the oral solution to a child, shake the bottle well before each use and use the provided measuring cup to ensure accurate dosing. Continue taking stavudine even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. Missing doses or abruptly stopping the medication may make your condition harder to treat. Stavudine is sometimes used in combination with other medications to prevent HIV infection in healthcare workers or others accidentally exposed to the virus. Discuss the potential risks of using this medication for your condition with your doctor. It may also be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before taking stavudine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to stavudine or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking, especially those mentioned in the Important Warning section, as well as zidovudine (Retrovir, also found in combination products like Combivir and Trizivir). Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you closely for side effects. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had kidney disease, diabetes (if taking stavudine solution), or peripheral neuropathy (nerve damage causing tingling, numbness, and pain in the hands and feet). If you are breastfeeding, inform your doctor, as breastfeeding is not recommended if you are HIV-positive or taking stavudine. Be aware that stavudine can cause side effects requiring immediate treatment before they become severe. Children taking stavudine may not be able to communicate their side effects, so ask their doctor how to recognize serious symptoms. Additionally, note that your body fat may increase or redistribute to areas such as your breasts or upper back. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, continue your normal diet while taking stavudine. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Stavudine may cause mild side effects such as headaches or diarrhea. Inform your doctor if these symptoms are severe or persistent. Serious side effects include numbness, tingling, burning, or pain in the hands or feet, difficulty moving your hands or feet, or a rash. If you experience any of these, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects should also be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store stavudine capsules at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture, and keep them tightly closed and out of reach of children. Store the oral solution in the refrigerator and discard any unused portion after 30 days. Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call 911. Symptoms of overdose may include numbness, tingling, or pain in the hands or feet, difficulty moving the hands or feet, nausea, vomiting, unusual or unexpected abdominal pain, weakness or fatigue, shortness of breath, or weakness in the arms and legs. Do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
